pages.title: Welcome
pages.subtitle: What this planner is for

blocks.heading: This is a project planner, not a day planner
paragraphs: Some work cannot be finished in an afternoon. A book, a thesis, a codebase, a case, a course, a rebuild. Work of that size fails for one reason: it never gets a protected place in the week, so it is done in the gaps, and the gaps are never enough.

blocks.heading: The unit here is the campaign
paragraphs: You name one body of deep work. You commit a number of hours a week to it. You run it for thirteen weeks and you keep a record of what those hours actually produced. The planner is built around that arc, not around tomorrow.

blocks.heading: What it asks of you
items: One project at a time — a second project is the most common way the first one dies
A weekly hour target you can defend, not one that flatters you
A session log written at the end of every session, not from memory on Sunday
Twenty minutes a week for the review

blocks.heading: What it does not do
paragraphs: It will not make the work interesting on a bad day, and it will not manufacture hours your life does not contain. It will show you, in writing, where the hours went — which is the only thing that changes anything.

pages.title: Instructions
pages.subtitle: Set up in an hour, then run it weekly

blocks.heading: Choose your size
paragraphs: Four sizes are included and all four contain identical pages. A4 and US Letter suit the desk. A5 and Half Letter suit a tablet or a bag, and print two-up on a full sheet.

blocks.heading: Set up once
items: Read the Deep Work Method page
Name the project on a Deep Work Goals page and set the thirteen-week milestone
Run the Priority Matrix to confirm nothing else deserves the hours more
Fill the Focus Environment Checklist and make the changes before week one

blocks.heading: Every week
items: Weekly Planning: set the hour target and name the milestone for the week
Time Blocking Planner: shade the bands where the deep hours will actually sit
Run the sessions, logging each one as it ends
Weekly Review, then one line on the Progress Dashboard

blocks.heading: Digital use
items: Import the PDF as a document, not as an image
Switch to read mode to tap links, write mode to write
Use the Sessions tab to reach the log from anywhere

pages.title: Deep Work Method
pages.subtitle: Five rules the structure is built on

blocks.heading: Depth is a capacity, not a mood
paragraphs: The ability to hold a hard problem for three hours is trained, and it decays. Most people attempting deep work start at forty minutes and are disappointed. Start where you are and extend the block by fifteen minutes a fortnight.

blocks.heading: Schedule the hours before the week starts
paragraphs: Deep work placed in whatever time is left over receives whatever attention is left over. The Time Blocking Planner is filled on Sunday, not on Wednesday morning.

blocks.heading: One project, thirteen weeks
items: A second project halves the first and finishes neither
Thirteen weeks is long enough to show a trend and short enough to stay real
The milestone is written before week one, not discovered in week nine

blocks.heading: Record output, not hours
paragraphs: Hours logged reward endurance. The session log asks what was produced, because four hours that moved nothing is information you need.

blocks.heading: Shallow work is not the enemy
paragraphs: Email, admin and meetings are the job too. They are only a problem when they are unbounded. Batch them, give them a slot, and stop treating them as a moral failure.
